claims.text: Inert gas condensation produces near-equiatomic MnFeCoNiCu solid-solution nanoparticles with minimal initial elemental segregation.
A controlled mild oxidative pretreatment can form a uniform, defect-minimized, ultrathin oxide layer on MnFeCoNiCu nanoparticles.
The oxide formed by the pretreatment is self-limiting.
The passivation layer is enriched in oxidation-prone elements such as Mn and Cu.
The passivation layer suppresses elemental segregation during high-temperature cycling.
The passivation layer suppresses surface diffusion and nanoparticle sintering during high-temperature operation.
Differences in elemental oxidation tendencies drive surface segregation and elemental mobility under operating conditions.
Controlled oxidation pins the nanoparticle surface composition and prevents further diffusion.
Controlled oxide passivation prevents phase decomposition.
Oxide passivation mitigates the enthalpic driving force for segregation and thereby stabilizes the nanoparticle's high-configurational-entropy state.
Oxidatively pretreated nanoparticles will retain a single-phase solid solution better than reducing-condition controls after thermal cycling.
Oxidatively pretreated nanoparticles will show less elemental segregation than reducing-condition controls.
Improved structural integrity will preserve catalytic turnover frequency and selectivity.
Improved structural integrity will preserve thermoelectric performance.
Reducing-condition baseline nanoparticles lack an effective oxide passivation layer.
Reducing-condition baseline nanoparticles undergo greater segregation and phase instability under the same service conditions.
Nonuniformity or defects in the oxide layer can cause localized degradation.
Changes in synthesis method or oxidation parameters can alter passivation efficacy.

contradictions.description: The baseline is described as being maintained under strictly reducing conditions, but the conditions field says both sets undergo alternating mildly oxidizing and reducing atmospheres. Thus the intended control atmosphere is not internally consistent.
